reasons: Section 1.4 is the only inbound grant (access to and right to use HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools) and names only 'the Company', with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice mechanism to add them — this fails the fallback ('affiliates covered on written notice') on a material term, so 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than compliant-at-fallback.

The redline is additive and surgical: it appends one sentence extending the Section 1.4 access and use rights to Company affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, leaving the original service and bandwidth commitments untouched. The failed 'minimal edit' check is an artefact of the appended sentence's length relative to a short paragraph, not a rewrite of existing terms.

Successor transfer is correctly treated as already satisfied by Section 10.3 (binding on successors and assigns), and the outbound Marks licence in Section 6.1 is properly not flagged because it benefits us — no double-flagging or flagging of favourable terms.
Comment is accurate, cites the playbook position, explains the operational reason (our web/IT providers need tool access) and offers the written-notice fallback; tone and prefix conform.

Minor over-reach to flag in negotiation but not disqualifying: the added 'not revocable or suspendable by HDI' goes slightly beyond the rule's 'delete revocable' guidance (the clause had no at-will revocation) and 'suspendable' could cut across HDI's remedies for non-payment; consider narrowing to 'not revocable at HDI's discretion' or 'except for uncured material breach'.
